sectors.name: Technology
themes: US AI capex cycle remains the dominant demand driver for NVDA and ANET, with hyperscaler spending durability underpinning multi-quarter earnings revisions despite rate volatility.
Indonesian digital economy names (MSKY, IKBI) face structural headwinds from high local funding costs and consumer purchasing-power compression, capping valuation multiples versus global peers.
Pricing-power software franchises like FICO and SHOP are re-rating on recurring revenue resilience, but their gains are increasingly idiosyncratic, not sector-wide, as macro dispersion widens.
sectors.ai: Buy selective large-cap AI infrastructure (NVDA, ANET) and platform winners (SHOP) on dips; trim small-cap Indonesian tech (MSKY, IKBI) into strength as US rates stay sticky and IDX tech liquidity thins. Watch FICO for sustained pricing power, but avoid chasing post-earnings gaps. Net: stay underweight sector, overweight AI hardware and global SaaS leaders with cash-flow visibility.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's geothermal expansion is structurally underpinned by state-mandated capacity targets and PLN's grid integration, making PGEO a durable compounder regardless of global clean-tech sentiment.
Green ammonia and downstream petrochemical conversion at TPIA position it as a multi-decade beneficiary of Japan/Korea hydrogen import demand, insulated from short-term US rate cycles.

Domestic renewables outperform US peers due to rupiah-stable cash flows and government subsidies, but policy execution risk (permitting, land acquisition) remains the key swing factor for smaller caps
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesia renewable names on dips: PGEO and NRG lead on geothermal and gas-to-power momentum, while TPIA's green ammonia optionality adds upside. The sector's local resilience (+0.12% ID vs -2.17% US) signals domestic policy tailwinds outweigh global rate fears. Accumulate PGEO and TPIA; avoid BREN until clarity on tariff reforms.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap FMCG names are driving sector returns as institutional investors rotate out of large-cap staples into higher-beta consumer plays with clearer earnings catalysts.
Water and beverage companies (ADES, AGAR) are benefiting from structural demand growth in premium hydration and on-the-go consumption, supported by rising urban disposable income.
Packaging and plastics-linked consumer firms (PDES, INDR) are gaining on input-cost stabilization and export-driven volume recovery, offering durable margin expansion into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small/mid-cap FMCG names showing volume-price breakouts (PDES, ADES, AGAR) while large caps lag; momentum is broad but fragile, so take profits on 10%+ single-day spikes. Favor water/beverage and packaging sub-sectors for earnings visibility; avoid chasing BTEK without confirmation. Position for a 2-4 week hold as IDX consumer breadth improves, but trim if aggregate signal flips negative.

themes: Indonesia's new capital project (IKN) is entering its peak construction phase, funneling sustained contracts to domestic contractors like SOLA and IPOL through 2025.
Gas infrastructure names (RGAS) benefit from the government's downstreaming mandate and rising industrial gas demand, a multi-year structural tailwind independent of global commodity cycles.
Cement (SMGR) is leveraging the housing deficit program and toll-road expansion, with pricing power improving as oversupply normalizes and logistics costs ease.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in SOLA, IPOL, and RGAS as their outsized gains reflect genuine order-flow catalysts in toll roads and gas distribution, not beta. SMGR's steady advance signals cement demand is firming ahead of the election-year infrastructure push. Trim US-exposed names like VRT on rate-cut delays; rotate into domestic contractors with visible government backlog.

RNAi and genetic medicine platforms (ALNY) are gaining clinical and commercial traction, creating a long-term moat in rare disease and cardiovascular indications.

Indonesia healthcare lags on macro, so rotate capital to US names for 3-6 months; avoid ID exposure until rupiah stabilizes.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's domestic logistics demand is decoupling from US weakness, driven by robust inter-island trade and government infrastructure spending on ports and toll roads.
Shipping and tanker names (SHIP, BLTA) are gaining from elevated coal and palm oil export volumes, a structural trend tied to China and India's commodity appetite.
Consolidation in the freight forwarding segment favors larger players like GTSI and ELPI, as smaller operators face margin compression from fuel costs and digitalization pressures.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in LOPI, TAXI, and GTSI on domestic volume resilience; US logistics weakness is a sentiment drag, not an Indonesia demand signal. Rotate out of laggards like BLTA and SAFE into names with port/commodity exposure. Expect consolidation near current levels, but add on any 3-5% dip as ID logistics outperformance persists through Q3.

Foreign capital rotation into Indonesian real estate is accelerating as US rate expectations stabilize, favoring liquid, well-governed developers over illiquid small caps.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Gold-backed stablecoins (PAXG, XAUT) are gaining structural traction as Indonesian investors hedge rupiah volatility and global macro uncertainty, creating durable demand for tokenized precious metals
DeFi protocol tokens like UNI benefit from persistent on-chain trading volume growth across Southeast Asian exchanges, with Indonesia's young, mobile-first user base driving adoption.
High-volatility altcoins (PI, LIT) see sharp but short-lived spikes from airdrop and listing events, signaling speculative retail flows that rotate quickly rather than build lasting positions.
sectors.ai: Rotate into gold-backed tokens (PAXG, XAUT) and high-beta altcoins (PI, UNI) as crypto aggregates stay flat; Indonesia's retail flow favors liquid, yield-bearing assets over speculative L1s.
